newsitem.title: FRANCE: Yemen official slams US on Iraq but woos Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Yemen official slams US on Iraq but woos Kuwait.

text.p: Yemen's parliamentary speaker denounced on Friday U.S. military threats against Iraq but said he wanted to help normalise ties with Kuwait, broken off when Yemen backed Baghdad's 1990 invasion of the oil-rich nation.

Threats by Washington to take military action against Iraq after Baghdad fired on U.S. surveillance planes "are unfair. We ask the United States to be just", Sheikh Abdullah Bin Hussein Al-Ahmar said.

"The hostile action launched by the Americans against Iraq was reprehensible," he said during a wide-ranging news conference near the end of a visit to Paris at the invitation of French parliamentary leaders.
"In our opinion, the United States intervened in a country's internal affairs. Iraq did nothing wrong, but was taking care of a problem on its own territory."
But Ahmar said he was willing to take the lead in an effort to restore ties with Kuwait, broken off after Yemen sided with Iraq following its invasion of Kuwait.
"There is a long history between the two countries. Differences should not go on too long," he said.

"I am ready to lead a parliamentary delegation or carry out a personal visit intended to re-establish relations with Kuwait...I am prepared to undertake such a visit when Kuwait wishes to receive it," he said.

Ahmar declined comment on Yemen's dispute with Eritrea over a group of small Red Sea islands, saying the matter was under international arbitration. But he went out of his way to say he personally blamed Israel for the confrontation.
"I accuse Israel of being behind the problem Yemen is having with Eritrea," he said.
Eritrean Marine Resources Minister Saleh Meki recently denied any Israeli role in his country's dispute over the potentially oil- and gas-rich Hanish islands.
At least 12 people were killed when Yemen and Eritrea briefly clashed over the islands last December.
Asked whether he had personally blocked a Yemeni bid to normalise ties with Israel, Ahmar flatly denied that such an initiative had ever been taken.

"There was never a push to normalise relations with Israel, and no one in Yemen dare bring up this subject," he said. "As you know, we condemn all those who have reconciled with Israel. So why should we want to imitate them?"

Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres told reporters in Paris in January that he had met Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh during memorial ceremonies for the late French president Francois Mitterrand and that Saleh had told him Yemen might normalise relations with Israel if Syria did so.
Yemeni officials quickly denied the account.
